sources.name: GeoNode maintainer security advisory
sources.data_date: Affected <=5.0.1; maintainer patched-version field is None

sources.name: GitHub reviewed GeoNode advisory
sources.data_date: Database lists <5.1.0 affected and 5.1.0 fixed; differs from maintainer metadata

sources.name: GeoNode upstream fix commit
sources.data_date: Commit 1408290c0bb54872924a9b334a516db9758a2180, referenced by the reviewed advisory

facts.statement: Arbitrary OS commands can be executed on the GeoNode by uploading a vector file with a crafted layer name.

editorial.title: GeoNode vector-upload layer names can trigger server-side command injection
editorial.summary: GeoNode’s maintainer reports command execution through crafted vector-upload layer names. Its advisory lists versions through 5.0.1 as affected. GitHub’s reviewed database lists 5.1.0 as fixed, while the maintainer’s patched-version field remains unset.
editorial.why_it_matters: The uploaded layer name reaches an operating-system command boundary. The source metadata disagrees on release coverage, so a database fixed-version entry alone should not establish a safe deployment.
editorial.action: Restrict untrusted vector uploads while checking the upstream fix and release coverage. Confirm the patch is present in the deployed GeoNode build before restoring that upload path.
